fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Patio Area; Perimeter Fencing; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of the street.
• Mark the single driveway access point clearly so responding units can identify it quickly from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach the main residence without obstruction.
• Identify and mark a secondary path to the rear of the property so responders are not dependent solely on the front driveway to reach all structures.
• Keep any gate or access point serving the rear of the property unlocked or secured with a knox-box style lock accessible to emergency responders.
• Trim dense vegetation along the driveway and walkways to maintain a clear path wide enough for responders carrying equipment on foot.
• Cut back vegetation that obscures sight lines between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can visually confirm both buildings on arrival.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without forcing through overgrowth.
• Post a property diagram near the front entrance showing the location of both structures, the patio area, and any rear access points.
• Keep the parking area organized so arriving emergency vehicles have a clear staging area near the front of the property.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Vegetation Along Driveway; Mixed Vegetation; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters closest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim branches on large trees that extend directly over or toward the structure.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees so fire cannot move easily between them.
• Clear ground vegetation growing beneath tree clusters near the structure.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation growing along the driveway edges to keep the travel path clear.
• Remove or thin shrubs growing close to the driveway that could block movement or visibility.
• Keep the area under scattered trees near the structure free of dead leaves, dry grass, and loose plant material.
• Maintain the open green space areas by keeping grass cut short, especially nearest the structure.
